quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, what does it mean?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of turn signals to show their intentions. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: Experienced riders use "SIPDE" to stay aware of conditions around them. What does the "P" stand for?

options.text: Prepare
Predict
Place
Position

questions.correctAnswerText: Predict
questions.explanation: SIPDE is a five-step process experienced riders use to make decisions while riding. The letters stand for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle.
Avoid crossing the tracks.
Cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.
Slowly inch across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: To safely cross railroad tracks or pavement seams, cross them at an angle of at least 45 degrees. Make a quick, sharp turn. Inching across slowly can cause the tracks to catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Just behind the lead rider.
At the back of the group.
Anywhere within the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front of the group, just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use sudden pressure on the front brake to prevent the front tire from locking.
Only use the rear brake.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the brake lever gradually to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: When may you not need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When the road is slippery
When there is a lot of traffic
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
When it is raining

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs longer to stop. Increase it if the road is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, where should you position yourself in your lane?

options.text: In the center portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
It does not matter where you are in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Being too close to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a collision.

questions.question: When may you not need a larger cushion of space around your motorcycle?

options.text: When the pavement is slippery
When you cannot see through the vehicle ahead
When weather and traffic conditions are perfect
When traffic is heavy

questions.correctAnswerText: When weather and traffic conditions are perfect
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in poor conditions. You need more space if the pavement is slippery, you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What is the best protection for a rider?

options.text: Space between your motorcycle and other vehicles
A good leather jacket
Sturdy boots
Knowledge of motorcycle laws

questions.correctAnswerText: Space between your motorcycle and other vehicles
questions.explanation: Your first and best protection is keeping distance from other vehicles. Space gives you time to react to other drivers' mistakes. Wearing proper protective gear is also important.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Bright colors like red, orange, yellow, and green make you more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: How do you stop with maximum braking power?

options.text: Using the rear brake only.
Using the front brake only.
Using both brakes.
Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together. Do not lock either wheel. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Using only the front brake
Using both brakes
Using the center lane
Maintaining or increasing your speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and use both brakes. Avoid sudden movements. Stay away from the center of the lane and follow tire tracks from cars. Watch for oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: When being passed, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
You may prevent another vehicle from passing you.
The portion of the lane nearest the passing vehicle is better.
You are more likely to experience a wind blast from the passing vehicle on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane may encourage the passing driver to return too soon. There may not be enough space.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Increase your ability to see.
Avoid placing you in other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Provide you with an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see better, avoid blind spots, escape wind blasts and hazards, and discourage sharing. It should NOT encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is too close to the car ahead.
A parked car has someone in the driver's seat.
You want people to look at your motorcycle.
You are passing a pedestrian in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to alert others before passing. Sound it if a driver is tailgating, if someone is in a parked car, or if a pedestrian is in the street. Do not use your horn just to get attention.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one, then the other.
Do both at the same time.
Always apply the brakes first, then swerve.
Try instead to use only the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake first, then swerve, or swerve first, then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: Why should you not change gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Your motorcycle may stall.
You might go too fast.
Other drivers may not be expecting you to change gears.
The uneven surface may make it more difficult to switch gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle could stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need in traffic?

options.text: Much less distance to stop than cars.
Less distance to stop than cars.
As much distance to stop as cars.
More distance to stop than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: As much distance to stop as cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars in traffic.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a motorcycle rider do?

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Use the horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Do not ride at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle so their headlights light you up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes slowing down, increasing your distance from other vehicles, using the headlights of cars ahead to see farther, using your high beam (unless a car is ahead or coming toward you), and changing your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.

options.text: 20 percent
40 percent
60 percent
80 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes many motorcycle crashes, especially deadly ones. Studies show that about 40 percent of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: When weight moves to the front of your bike during braking, you should:

options.text: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Not worry. Weight transfer does not affect your motorcycle.
Lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: As you brake, slowly add more pressure to the front brake lever. The bike's weight shifts forward to the front tire, so you need more front brake pressure.

questions.question: If rain starts while you are riding, what is a good idea?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Speed up.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil deposits and is dangerous when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Always slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride with your headlight on.
Reduce your distance from other vehicles.
Weave back and forth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at intersections to be more visible. Ride in a lane position that makes it easy for oncoming traffic to see you. Keep a safe distance so you can take action if needed. Do not assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.
